title: How many? A number and a singular noun

sections.title: Counting rooms and things
sections.content: After a number or *sok* (“many”), the noun stays singular. There is no plural *-k*, because the number already says “more than one”: *három szoba*, *sok ablak*. Ask “how many” with *hány*: *Hány szoba van a lakásban?* The answer can start with the place: *A lakásban három szoba van.*

items.english: How many rooms are there in the flat?
There are three rooms in the flat.
There are many windows in the house.
There are five chairs in the room.

sections.content: English adds an -s after a number: “three chairs”. Hungarian does not: *három szék*, never *három székek*. The same goes for *sok*.
